subject: Microbiology
subtopic: Toxoplasma gondii: life cycle, transmission, congenital disease and immunocompromised disease
concept: Toxoplasmosis is caused by the intracellular protozoan Toxoplasma gondii; cats are definitive hosts.

content.definition: Humans acquire infection mainly from tissue cysts in undercooked meat, environmental oocysts, or congenital transmission.
content.explanation: Tachyzoites disseminate during acute infection and later form persistent tissue cysts containing bradyzoites.
content.mechanism: Reactivation of latent cysts in immunocompromised patients can cause severe CNS or ocular disease; maternal primary infection can transmit to the fetus.
content.structure: Important forms include tachyzoites, bradyzoites within tissue cysts and environmental oocysts.
content.function: The life cycle between felids and intermediate hosts permits environmental and foodborne transmission.
causes: Contaminated soil, food or water containing oocysts
Rare transmission through blood or transplanted organs
effects: Often asymptomatic or mild in immunocompetent people
content.diagnosis: Toxoplasma-specific IgG and IgM are commonly used; PCR and specialized testing are used in selected congenital or immunocompromised cases.
content.treatment: Most healthy immunocompetent people recover without treatment. When treatment is indicated, pyrimethamine with sulfadiazine and folinic acid is a standard regimen; alternatives depend on clinical context.
high_yield: Toxoplasma gondii is an intracellular protozoan
Tachyzoite is the active multiplying form
Congenital and immunocompromised disease are major clinical concerns

terminology.etymology: Tachy means rapid; zoite refers to a living cell form.

yemen_context.relevance: Relevant to parasitology and hematology teaching; no unsupported Yemen-specific incidence is asserted.

review_notes: Original synthesis based on CDC clinical overview and care guidance.
